content.value_statement: Teams often add heavy libraries before a React app proves it needs them. This skill guides targeted TanStack adoption after vanilla code works.
actual_capabilities: Identifies TanStack Query candidates for caching, refetching, pagination, and optimistic updates.
Evaluates when TanStack Table can replace complex sorting, filtering, and pagination logic.
Distinguishes simple forms and tables that should remain vanilla.
Provides staged prompts for broad and focused TanStack analysis.
Encourages bundle size, team familiarity, and maintainability checks before adoption.
limitations: It does not install TanStack packages or modify files by itself.
It depends on an existing React or Next.js project for useful analysis.
It cannot guarantee performance gains without measurement.
It gives decision guidance, not official TanStack documentation.

use_cases.title: Plan React Refactors
use_cases.description: Review a working app and choose TanStack changes that reduce repeated state management.

use_cases.title: Control Library Sprawl
use_cases.description: Decide when vanilla React remains simpler than adding another dependency.

use_cases.title: Prepare Migration Tickets
use_cases.description: Turn approved Query, Table, Form, or Virtual candidates into scoped implementation tasks.

prompt_templates.title: Basic Adoption Review
prompt_templates.prompt: Analyze this working React or Next.js app for TanStack opportunities. List candidates, benefits, complexity, and what to keep vanilla.

prompt_templates.title: Query Candidate Scan
prompt_templates.prompt: Find data fetching code that may benefit from TanStack Query. Prioritize caching, refetching, pagination, and optimistic update cases.

prompt_templates.title: Table And Form Review
prompt_templates.prompt: Review forms, tables, and long lists. Recommend TanStack Form, Table, or Virtual only when current complexity justifies it.

prompt_templates.title: Migration Plan
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a staged migration plan for approved TanStack changes. Include risks, tests, rollback points, and bundle-size checks.

output_examples.input: Review a dashboard with repeated loading states, user refetching, and local filters.
output: Recommend TanStack Query for user data because caching and shared loading state are repeated.
Keep the small settings form vanilla because validation is simple.
Review the largest table separately before adding TanStack Table.

output_examples.input: Evaluate a customer table with sorting, filtering, pagination, and row selection.
output: TanStack Table is a strong candidate because several table behaviors are already custom-built.
Migration should start with column definitions and row selection tests.
Avoid TanStack Router because Next.js routing is already sufficient.

best_practices: Start from a working vanilla implementation before recommending TanStack.
Adopt one TanStack library at a time and measure the result.
Keep simple static tables, simple forms, and one-time fetches vanilla.
anti_patterns: Installing every TanStack library before clear needs are visible.
Replacing simple React code only because a library exists.
Ignoring bundle size, tests, and team familiarity during migration.

faq.question: Should I install every TanStack package first?
faq.answer: No. The skill recommends adoption only after a working vanilla version shows clear complexity or performance needs.

faq.question: Can it replace a code review?
faq.answer: No. It helps plan refactors, but engineers should verify behavior, tests, accessibility, and bundle impact.

faq.question: Does it work with Next.js App Router?
faq.answer: Yes. It often keeps App Router and recommends TanStack Router only when routing complexity justifies it.

faq.question: Will it modify my files automatically?
faq.answer: No. It provides analysis prompts and migration guidance. File edits require a separate implementation request.

faq.question: Which libraries does it cover?
faq.answer: It covers Query, Table, Form, Router, Virtual, and Ranger at a decision level.

faq.question: Can it help legacy React apps?
faq.answer: Yes. It can identify high-value candidates before a staged migration.
